# Quantum Distributed Addressed Phases

This repository gives a compiler for a coherent distributed addressed phase and
quantifies the Bell-pair requirements for interactive and simultaneous classical
communication. The data tables are explicit quantum registers at the modules.

## Scientific and learning routes

- Start at README.md for the results, a numerical example and the checks.
- Use science/model.md for the gate definition, references, Bell-pair budget,
  diamond norm convention and scope of each communication model.
- Use science/interactive-tree.md for the reversible address routing, exact
  hard-budget error formula and the matching Choi-state lower bound.
- Use science/simultaneous-exchange.md for the exact phase-column bound, the
  fixed-error bound and the two-module, one-exchange construction.
- Use learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md and learning/MILESTONES.md for a textbook bridge
  and the ordered project study route.
- Run the two Python commands in README.md for finite exact-arithmetic checks.
  Those checks test protocol branches and the discrete identities used in the
  tree frontier. The general bounds are proved in the science pages.

## Distinctions to preserve

- The hard Bell-pair cap applies per edge and per execution. Modules hold
  the tables explicitly and communicate through classical messages.
- The error is half diamond distance between unconditional channels, including
  inputs with references. The ideal Kraus weight is a component of the
  unconditional channel.
- The exact interactive result holds on all trees with at least two modules.
  The one-exchange lower bounds apply across each cut with one simultaneous
  classical exchange. The matching-order one-exchange upper bound is bipartite.
- The separation grows exponentially in address length k and linearly in table
  size 2^k. The link model assumes ideal Bell pairs and charges only their count.
